name: James Blair
currentRole: White House Deputy Chief of Staff
lane: Legislative, political and intergovernmental access coordination
accessTo: White House legislative, political and intergovernmental offices
constraints: Congress and state governments are independent constitutional actors
Political liaison is not command
Role may change with White House staffing
strongestCounterargument: The office can shape access and coalition management, but cannot control legislators, governors or voters.

name: Alexei Dyumin
currentRole: Aide to the President of Russia and Secretary of the State Council
lane: Presidential access, regional coordination and security background
accessTo: Security Council membership and regional leadership channels
constraints: Aide status is delegated
The State Council has defined constitutional and administrative functions
Prior security service does not prove current covert command
strongestCounterargument: His background and access are notable, but public evidence does not establish an autonomous power centre.

name: Boris Vujčić
currentRole: Vice-President of the European Central Bank
lane: Monetary-policy preparation and central-bank executive governance
accessTo: ECB Governing Council and national central banks
documentedReach: Implementation instructions to national central banks
constraints: Governing Council decisions are collective
Treaty mandate and courts constrain action
No fiscal or national-government authority
strongestCounterargument: The role is central to preparation and execution, but cannot unilaterally determine euro-area monetary policy.

name: Philip R. Lane
currentRole: Member of the Executive Board of the European Central Bank
mechanisms: Preparation and implementation of monetary decisions
Access to central-bank analysis and national-central-bank coordination
constraints: Collective decision-making
No personal ownership of monetary infrastructure
Treaty and judicial constraints
strongestCounterargument: Analytical influence can be important, but evidence must distinguish advice and preparation from final collective decisions.

name: Thomas E. Donilon
currentRole: Vice Chairman of BlackRock and Chairman of the BlackRock Investment Institute
lane: Geopolitical analysis and former national-security network bridge
mechanisms: Chairs geopolitical and macro research platform
constraints: No current government command
Former classified access does not establish current classified access
Research views do not automatically control portfolios or policy
strongestCounterargument: His background creates expertise and relationships, but current influence must be shown through documented actions rather than inferred from former office.

name: Adebayo Ogunlesi
currentRole: Chairman and CEO of Global Infrastructure Partners; BlackRock board member and Global Executive Committee member
constraints: Individual assets have separate owners, boards and regulators
Board service is not operational command
Investment management is bound by fund mandates
strongestCounterargument: Cross-board reach is a meaningful access mechanism but does not establish unified control of infrastructure or technology companies.

name: Mohamed Mazyed Al-Tuwaijri
currentRole: Advisor at the Saudi Royal Court and member of the PIF Board of Directors
accessTo: Mohammed bin Salman as PIF chair
constraints: Board decisions are collective
Executive management implements investments
No evidence of authority outside delegated Saudi institutions
strongestCounterargument: The combination of court and board access is significant, but does not establish private control of state policy or investments.

name: Maxim Oreshkin
currentRole: Deputy Chief of Staff of the Presidential Executive Office of Russia
constraints: Role is delegated
Finance and economic institutions have separate mandates
Public title does not reveal every internal assignment
strongestCounterargument: The position creates access but does not prove personal control of Russia's economy or central bank.
